content.thinking:
I'm planning the full elf archer rig in one pass, mapping out the skeleton structure—hips, spine, neck, head, jaw, arms, legs—plus accessories like a cloak, ponytail chain, quiver, and bow, and working out the standing pose coordinates before writing the final file.

Still defining the spine and neck chains...

Setting loft stations for pelvis, waist, chest, and shoulders with matching widths and heights, aligned to the spine path. Then planning torso paint as a forest green tunic with gold trim and brown leather accents, using cel shading with ink outlines.

Now I'm settling on the character's palette — silver-blonde hair with teal highlights, teal-green cloak, gold accents, and emerald-gold eyes — keeping the total flat colors under 64 while relying mostly on cel-shaded paints. For the arm rig, I'm placing shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints and deciding on a neutral A-pose with arms extended apart for the rest position, considering whether the left hand should hold a bow.

Setting sweep radii for the arm, planning sleeve coverage on the upper arm in tunic color and leaving the forearm bare skin with a bracer accent.

The limb chain gives root, elbow, wrist as three points with the path ending at the wrist target, so I'll build the hand as a palm sphere plus simple capsule fingers rather than detailed gloves, keeping it skin-toned and minimal.

For the hand holding the bow, I'm positioning the grip near the hand target with fingers hanging downward as short rods, then placing the bow vertically in the sideways plane at the character's side—checking that its lowered tip doesn't dip below floor level or collide with the leg.

I'm working out the bow's curvature with the limbs bending backward relative to the grip and the string running straight between the tips, figuring out which direction the belly should face.

I need to figure out the hand bone for attaching the bow: with only three joint names per arm (shoulder, elbow, wrist), the wrist acts as the tip joint, so I can reference the arm's tip directly as the hand bone to anchor the bow to.

Now for the bow string connecting tip to tip, I'm adding gold leaf ornaments on the limbs, a wrapped leather grip, spiked tips, and small glowing gems on the riser and brooch. For the quiver, I'm placing a diagonal leather tube on the back attached to the chest spine joint, with arrows represented as rods poking out from inside it.

Still writing arrow details...

Positioning the quiver diagonally over the right shoulder to the left hip, with the top end near the shoulder and bottom near the hip, checking clearance against the torso surface so it doesn't clip through the back. I'm also sketching out a draped strap across the chest using a closed curve of points following the torso surface.

Only the torso loft surface should be used, not the arms. For the belt, I'm planning a sweep loop near the hips using a point around the pelvis height with a slight lift, attaching the buckle and pouches to the hip bone for weighting. Now I'm thinking through how to shape the tunic's flared tails, possibly using a lathe for the skirt silhouette.

Writing extrude panel code...

I'll skip the rotation tilt and mirror the panel at the back. Thinking about whether to add a full cloak given the quiver placement, I decide to skip it and consider a simpler shoulder cape instead.

Positioning the cape outline behind the quiver so it doesn't clash, pushing it further back in depth so the quiver's arrows remain visible sticking out in front.

Actually, hanging the cape loose creates too big a gap from the torso, so I'll scrap that approach and instead go with a thin shoulder mantle that hugs the body closely rather than floating freely.

Attaching the cloak to the spine's chest joint for movement, then shifting focus to the head: building the skull as a scaled sphere, adding a separate cheek/chin sphere for facial contouring, and shaping a pointed chin using a downward-facing cone.

Now I'm working out the jaw as its own piece on a jaw bone, positioning a small chin sphere beneath the skull, and figuring out where the skull's front surface sits in space for placing decals. I'm planning eye placement as decals on the skull's surface using azimuth/elevation coordinates to position them correctly on the curved head shape.

Placing the mouth similarly—thin dark line using a tiny swept curve positioned low on the face, built from a few hit points sampled at small azimuth offsets around a steep downward elevation to form a subtle curved mouth shape.

For the jaw, I'm separating it as its own part from the skull since the mouth needs an upper and lower jaw. I'm sketching a chin sphere scaled and positioned near the lower face, but I'm noticing it overlaps with the skull's lower boundary, so I need to adjust the positioning to avoid that collision.

Still placing bone joints...

Now for the ears, I'm planning elongated elven points swept from the skull side using a bezier path from base to a curved outward tip.

Next I'm thinking through hair: a silvery long cap sweeping over the skull, oversized slightly to cover the scalp and back of the head.

But I realize the cap's coverage angle would also hide the forehead and eyes, so I need to tilt it backward so the face stays exposed and only the crown and back are covered.

Working out that back edge falls below horizontal to cover the nape, confirming the thetaLength value, then sketching the fringe/bangs as swept spike shapes projecting down from the forehead hit point toward the brow line, using spherical coordinates for the base and tip positions.

I'm defining a helper function that computes points on the skull surface from azimuth, elevation, and a scale factor, so I can place hair spikes without needing full surface queries -- planning to use it for both bangs and possibly eye placement, with five bang spikes positioned at specific azimuth angles.

For the side locks, I'm sketching bezier sweeps that start near the temples and curve down past the shoulders to the chest, tapering the radius from thicker at the base to thin at the tip, making sure the ends land in front of the chest rather than clipping through the shoulder geometry.

I'm also considering a back ponytail parented to the head, but worried it will intersect with the quiver and cloak, so I'm reworking it as a braid that drapes forward over one shoulder instead, starting at the nape and curving toward the front of the chest.

This math is getting too fiddly for precise placement, so I'll simplify: just route the ponytail/braid as a high arc starting from the back of the head, curving outward and down behind the shoulders toward the cloak area, rather than tracking exact ellipse intersections.

Adding a gold tie ring at the ponytail base and working out hair shading with a cel-shaded gradient and stripe highlights for a teal root effect.

I'm also designing a thin gold circlet around the skull with a green forehead gem, building it from a closed curve of head points at a fixed elevation so it wraps naturally over the hair.

Eyebrows get folded into the face decal, and I'm enlarging the elf eye decal dimensions. For clothing I'm sketching a tunic paint function: a gold centerline seam down the chest, and a lighter leather vest accent higher up, building toward a vest trim color scheme.

Writing torso paint function...

For the legs, I'm planning leather-fawn leggings with chain sweeps at varying radii, plus tall brown boots covering the lower leg with a three-point path from hip to knee to ankle.

I need a cuff ring at the boot boundary for a folded-leather look, maybe using a short rod between two chain points with flat gold caps to avoid radius discontinuity. Then for the foot, I'm thinking of building the boot's sole/toe as a separate box or loft shape extending forward from the ankle point.

I'm adding a toe cap and sole piece to the foot geometry, making sure the sole bottom sits flush with the floor at y=0, then checking the leg geometry so the ankle target height of 0.08 works with the hip position, allowing a slight knee bend forward.

I'm placing hip joints symmetrically with the spine chain rooted above, then sizing a leather bracer with gold trim rings around the forearm near the elbow, and sketching hemisphere pauldron plates on the shoulders oriented outward and up.

For the pauldrons I'm deciding between stacked hemisphere layers or a simpler hemisphere with a gold rim torus and gem accent, anchored to the shoulder joint. I'm also planning a teal scarf-like gorget swept around the neck as a thin torus, and considering a striped leaf-motif paint pattern for the teal cloak.

For the cloak surface, I'm thinking through a gradient-based cel shading from light to dark teal top to bottom, plus a gold hem trim near the bottom edge, possibly with a jagged leaf-tip silhouette instead of a straight hem. Rather than fight with procedural zigzag outlines, I'll simplify to the gradient shading and add a separate textured plane with a vine-and-leaf SVG pattern layered on the back of the cloak for visual detail.

I'll place that vine-leaf plane facing backward so it reads correctly from behind, and add a matching leaf emblem plane on the front tunic panel facing forward -- sharing one SVG-generating helper for the leaf motif. For extra flourish I'm considering small gold cone spikes as faux tassels on the belt, and gold leaf accents or small sphere "bands" distributed along the bow's limbs using a path-following helper, though I'll need to figure out how to space those along the bow's curve.

Now I'm working out how to attach those sphere bands along the bow path with correct bone weighting, and planning a small glowing green gem embedded at the bow's grip for a magical accent -- positioning it on the riser's front face.

Then I'm figuring out how the left hand grips the bow: a palm sphere centered at the grip plus a row of small curled finger blobs wrapping around the vertical riser axis, trying to get positions that look like fingers naturally curled around the grip.

Still building hand geometry...

Planning skin shading with a cel function and keeping imports trimmed to only what's actually used—cel, INK, animeEye, furEdge—to avoid unused-locals errors. Deciding to skip extra details like braids or ear tufts and move on to writing the actual component.

I'm setting up the meta info (name, description, style, commit) and starting the build function, picking a paint atlas size, then defining the hips joint as the root spine joint with its position.

Building the spine chain and neck chain...

Building each leg chain with hip, knee, and ankle joints, then sweeping them with pants and boot color bands covering the full length.

Now I'm defining the boot geometry as a frustum box attached to the ankle joint, working out which axis the box width should align with for a symmetrical foot shape.

Adding sole and toe geometry...

Now I'm working on the boot cuff with a tapered radius profile and a thin gold band rod at the top, followed by lace straps across the boot front.

Adding gold buckle rings next, placing small torus shapes along the leg's tangent direction at each strap position, matching their radius to the tube's taper so they sit snugly against the boot.

Now I'm working out the arm chains: shoulder, elbow, wrist joints per side, attaching them to the spine, with hand positions set to reach the bow grip at roughly x=0.45 so the arm bends slightly rather than fully extending. Building the limb sweep geometry...

Still positioning hand and finger geometry...

Working out finger capsule placement...

Now I'm adding a leather wrap rod where the hand grips, plus a quiver attached at the chest bone with tapered round-to-flat caps, and decorative gold ring bands spaced along its length.

I'm also scattering five arrows poking out from the quiver top, with slightly randomized offsets and spread so the shafts and tips fan out naturally rather than looking perfectly aligned.

Fletching feathers near the tips alternate teal and white with a nock cap at the end, while the arrowheads stay hidden inside the quiver. Now I'm working out the torso loft surface using the hip-to-spine bone chain for the path, and sketching tunic panels and a belt loop positioned around the hip joint.

Still refining belt dimensions...

Now I'm placing a hip pouch at the pelvis side, sized to fit within the pelvis half-width, with leather material plus a flap and gold stitching detail.

Then I'm adding a sheathed dagger on the hip with an angled sheath rod and hilt/pommel gem, positioned to balance the mirrored arm hang. I'm also planning asymmetrical shoulder pauldrons—left larger with gold trim, right smaller—and a teal scarf ring around the neck built from an elliptical set of points swept into a tube.

For the scarf, I'm attaching it to the neck bone and adding a front knot with two hanging ribbon tails extruded from a chest point, shaped with a sharp taper at the bottom, matching the torso's z-depth near the vest. Then I move to face details—nose, mouth, and brow decals, elvish cheekbones—and start building the skull as a scaled sphere geometry attached to the head bone.

For the eyes, I'm computing symmetric hit points on the skull surface at a mirrored angle on each side, then placing eye decals there sized to leave a small gap between them for a stylized anime look, deciding to keep the projection direction straight ahead rather than following the surface normal so the eyes don't look distorted.

Now I'm checking the vertical placement—adjusting the eye elevation downward to sit in the lower-mid portion of the skull, verifying it doesn't clip past the chin or hairline, then moving on to position a small nose sphere lower on the face.

Checking the chin cone geometry, it seems to stick out too far from the face, so I'm reworking the lower face as a scaled jaw sphere with a separate downward cone for the chin instead.

For the mouth, rather than computing complex surface intersections between skull and jaw parts, I'll simplify by casting rays from fixed points toward the face to find where they hit, placing small dark mouth segments at those computed surface coordinates across a few x positions.

I'm checking whether the jaw face sphere overlaps the skull surface near the eye region, comparing their radii and positions along y and z to see if the lower-face mesh might improperly cover the eyes.

I'm sketching the chin as a cone attached to the jaw bone, pointing down and slightly forward, then working out ear geometry as a bezier path curving backward and upward from the side of the skull to form pointed elf-style ears.

For the ear shape, I'm defining a radius function that tapers from a wider flattened oval base down to a thin point at the tip, uncertain about the exact orientation but leaning toward flattening the ear along one axis for a more natural look, possibly with an inner pink layer for detail.

For the hair cap, I'm positioning a partial sphere scaled into an oval shape, placed near the top of the head and tilted backward slightly to sit naturally like a cap, working through the rotation math to get the tilt angle correct.

Cap radius checks out against skull volume. I want to add extra hair volume with back/side tufts and spike blades hanging from the cap rim down the nape, stopping short of the ponytail. The forehead circlet ornament looks fine, and now I'm positioning the cloak extrusion behind the torso, working out its z-depth and thickness relative to the shoulder and chest curve.

I'm checking that the quiver's radius doesn't collide with the cloak depth, nudging its z position slightly back to clear it. Then I'm defining the cloak's outline points from the shoulders down to the sharp-pointed hem tails, confirming it hangs well above the ground and clears the back of the thighs and legs.

I'm deciding to use smoothing 0 rather than 1 for the cloak outline to avoid any risk of corner-cutting crossing the sharp hem tips, opting for more points over smoothed curves for safety. Now I'm working out the hem trim pattern, using the paint distance function to create a zigzag gold leaf band along the lower edge of the cloak.

I'm planning the paint logic to give edge walls a gold frame while the face gets a dark teal band with a zigzag hem pattern and subtle vertical fold stripes using a sine wave. Finally I'm adding a gold clasp/brooch detail at the chest-front neckline position with a glowing gem disk.

Also adding a thin gold center stripe for trim, then designing an SVG leaf emblem decal with veins and a curl to place on the tunic.

Finishing SVG code...

Now placing it as a decal plane positioned just above the panel surface so it sits flush on the front face without clipping into the back.

For the cloak, I'm sketching a larger vine SVG with leaves branching off a central stem, then mapping it onto a plane sized to the cloak's center and oriented to face outward correctly for the viewer. I'm wiring up a helper that builds a textured plane part with position, facing direction, and bone attachment, then moving on to add glowing gem accents on the brooch, circlet, bow, and dagger pommel.

Now I'm sketching smaller details like the quiver strap, belt, and bracers, deciding to skip extras like lacing rods and buttons for simplicity, and planning the ponytail using a swept chain with a gradient hair color. I'm also adding seven bang spikes for the forelock and reminding myself to always specify colors explicitly to avoid default coloring issues. With part counts around 120, I'm defining a helper function that computes 3D positions on the head using azimuth and elevation angles for consistent hair/accessory placement.

Working out bang spike geometry, adjusting their length and curvature so the tips don't overlap the eyes but still rest naturally near the brow line.

For the side hair locks, I'm mapping out curved paths from the temple down past the neck toward the shoulder, using a tapering radius along the curve.

Now I'm sketching the ponytail as a chain of hair segments trailing behind the head, curving back and down, but I need to check whether it collides with the quiver strapped to the back since both occupy similar depth and height near the shoulders.

Still positioning the hair tie, then adding a gold circlet sweep and defining the toon eye material with its iris colors.

Checking stroke widths scale properly at the raster resolution, then applying glow effects to parts and verifying torus geometry. Now I'm sketching the cloak vine SVG with a winding stem path and leaf details.

Defining the paint constants next: skin tones, hair with striped shading, and a gradient treatment for swept hair strands.

Now I'm picking out the outfit palette — a green tunic, a dark brown vest, tan leggings, and brown boots — aiming for a ranger-like contrast scheme.

Adding a teal-blue cloak and gold accents for the color scheme, then I'm writing the shirt and vest paint function, defining a cream V-neck shirt under a brown vest with a gold edge line, calculating how the V-neck opening widens based on vertical position.

Still writing paint logic...

Adding quiver cap disc and arrow offsets...

I'm checking the hips-to-spine loft stations and joint positions align correctly, then confirming the eye decal targets the right surface. For the shoulder pauldron I'm placing an open hemisphere at the shoulder joint with a gold rim trim.

Adding the right-side dagger with its sheath, hilt grip, and crossguard positioned at the hip bone.

Now I'm figuring out the bowstring geometry, connecting the tips with a straight rod while accounting for the curve direction of the tips relative to the grip so the tension looks right.

Then I'm working out the catmull curve points for the bow's shape, mirroring the top and bottom halves symmetrically around the grip point.

Still writing bow geometry...

I need to make sure the bow is built after the arm loop so I can reference the left hand joint, so I'll store the hand joint reference before constructing the bow.

Still defining sweeps and geometry helpers...

I'm also planning cross-body strap draping and double-checking that every import—THREE, bezier, catmull, gradient, paint, zigzag, glow, and the rest—actually gets used somewhere in the final build, while skipping unnecessary pant and quiver details.

Now I'm working through part placement for a hemisphere shape and writing the eye decal logic with null-hit guards, plus assembling the face surface from skull, jaw, and chin parts and setting up mouth coordinate points.

Still writing facial detail logic...

Now I'm sweeping the neck chain with tapered skin radii, then adding a teal collar ring positioned around the neck joint before starting on scarf tail ribbons extruding from the chest.

Checking overall proportions: head-top height around 1.93 with hair cap, ears, and ponytail factored in, which fits a stylized elf scale, and confirming the sole sits at y=0. Hands are posed with the left gripping the bow and the right relaxed, so now I'm ready to write the final file.
